_about: Captured on the local bench with OPENCLAW_CAPTURE_FRAMES against OpenClaw 2026.10.33 (run 2026-11-24T22-39-08-086Z, the GO run of that version). Bench prompts only; no personal data. Each turn is the frames of ONE run as the bridge received them, in arrival order across its two sockets: `conversation` entries are the raw `chat` / `agent` frames of the run on one conversation socket, unmodified; `session-events` entries are the `session.message` events of the same session on the session-events socket, whose payload is reduced to sessionKey, sessionId, agentId, messageId, messageSeq, runId, hasActiveRun and the unmodified `message` (the session snapshot the event also carries is dropped: no reader of these rows uses it). `receivedAt` is the bridge's receive clock (ms). `longReply`: scenario basic-turn, a 544-character reply in 29 deltas; the row arrives 1 ms before the emptying delta, the final 26 ms after it. `toolsThenReply`: scenario media-outbound, tool calls then the reply; the run's two tool-call rows are recorded mid-run, the text row at the end. `rowAfterEmptying`: a widget turn where the text row arrives 1 ms AFTER the emptying delta. `messageToolRows`: scenario settle-message-tool-codemode, a requester-settle run whose two `message`-tool sends are recorded mid-run as visible delivery-mirror rows that withdraw nothing from the stream.

Il relie deux rives pour assurer la continuité d’une route.
Il facilite le déplacement des voyageurs et des marchands.
Il permet aux armées de traverser les obstacles naturels.
Ses arches transmettent le poids du tablier vers les piles et les culées.
Ses piles soutiennent la structure tout en laissant passer l’eau.
Son tablier offre une surface de passage aux piétons, aux animaux et aux véhicules.
Il favorise ainsi les échanges entre les territoires qu’il relie.

name: inline-widget-delivery
description: Render or decline requests for live inline HTML widgets in chat, including widget buttons that send follow-up prompts.
---

# Inline widget delivery

Use this when the user asks for an interactive/live HTML widget rendered inline in the current chat or transcript.

1. Check whether the current turn exposes the inline widget authoring tool (`show_widget` or an exact equivalent). Do this before building alternate hosting, dashboard, canvas, browser, or portal workarounds.
2. If the inline widget tool is available, call it once with a short `title` and self-contained `widget_code`. For buttons that report back to the chat, use the widget host prompt bridge, preferring `openclaw.prompt.send(text)` with a fallback to `sendPrompt(text)` when appropriate.
3. If the inline widget tool is not available, do not substitute `canvas`, `dashboard`, `[embed ...]`, browser hosting, or a portal as if they were the requested inline chat widget. State plainly that inline widget rendering is unavailable in this turn and, when the user asked for a tool inventory, list only the actually available matching tool names.
4. Keep probe widgets tiny and self-contained; avoid external assets unless the user requested them or the widget needs a pinned public library.

Completion check: either the inline widget tool accepted the widget code, or the reply clearly declined inline rendering without presenting a non-inline surface as equivalent.
